messages:
kevin: vuln-bot flagged CVE-2025-3117 in a transitive wheel (openvino) pulled in by our image-builder pipeline. looks like a false positive but want to get an exception while we confirm.

autobot-vuln: scanner: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-3117 severity: MEDIUM vector: NETWORK description: 'Potential stack overflow in openvino serialization' — reported in binary artifacts.

kevin: repro steps: inside the build container i ran `pipdeptree -w -l` and traced openvino -> onnxruntime-wheel -> manylinux wheel. the scanner is matching a symbol pattern in the openvino binary but the binary in package is stripped and CI builds use our hardened flags. snippet:```
$ pipdeptree | sed -n '1,40p'
openvino==2024.4.2
  - onnxruntime==1.15.2
  - numpy==1.24.3
```

kevin: also ran `readelf -s` and couldn't find the vulnerable symbol, only these exports: `ov_infer, ov_read_model` so looks like FP to me.

maria: thanks. can you attach the exact file the scanner pointed to and CI job id? we need those for the formal risk acceptance ticket.

kevin: attaching paths from the job: `gs://build-artifacts/redwood/image-builder/2026-06-12/openvino-2024.4.2-manylinux.whl` job: `ci/image-builder/5689`

kevin: quick ask: can sec grant a temporary allowlist of this path so downstream deploys aren't blocked while we triage? target window 72h. we'll push a rebuild with debug symbols + yara rule to confirm.

sam: quick questions on compensating controls: are the runtime images immutable and do we scan container runtime at deploy? if yes we can reduce blast radius.

kevin: yes — runtime images are signed via cosign and immutable. deploys go through gate that verifies signature and we run runtime vulnerability scan in staging. production rollout requires an additional manual approval for changes to image-builder artifacts.

lena: from infra side — we can add a temporary soft-fail rule in the scanner for that exact GCS path. need sec ownership + a vuln tracker link so we can auto-revert in 72h.

maria: propose steps: 1) sec creates an exception ticket with reason + artifact link + triage notes; 2) infra applies soft-fail allowlist for exactly that GCS path (no wildcard) for 72h; 3) eng/kevin to produce debug build demonstrating FP or patch; 4) sec sign-off to close exception. everyone ok?

kevin: yes. i'll add triage notes and a minimal reproducer (debug symbols and readelf outputs).

maria: tagging legal/compliance not necessary for this one (low severity + internal artifact), but i'll note it in the ticket. approve temp allowlist? :eyes:

sam: +1 from platform. please add mitigation notes: image immutability, signature verification, staging scans.

maria: created ticket SEC-2026-1123: temporary allowlist request for CVE-2025-3117 on openvino wheel. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-1123. infra please apply soft-fail to the path above and set reversion timer 72h.

kevin: thanks, infra applied soft-fail at 2026-06-12T14:32Z per ticket. i'll upload debug build within 6 hours.

autobot-vuln: note: auto-reminder set — this exception will expire 2026-06-15T14:32Z unless SEC-2026-1123 is updated.

lena: soft-fail applied. reversion scheduled. added a watcher to the ticket so infra will revert automatically.

kevin: uploaded debug build and readelf dumps to the ticket. analysis shows no matching unsafe symbol — looks like the yara signature matched a legacy pattern in the stripped artifact.

maria: thanks. i'll review the artifacts and if confirmed FP we will close SEC-2026-1123 and note the compensating controls. else we escalate.

sam: one more ask — can we add a quick regression test to the image-builder pipeline to detect this signature to avoid future noise?

kevin: yes, will add a unit job that runs the yara check against debug build and fail if it matches. PR incoming.

maria: closing loop: confirmed false positive. SEC-2026-1123 closed with disposition: temporary allowlist used during triage, compensating controls in place (image signing, immutable deploys, staging scans), follow-up: add regression job to image-builder, timeline: 72h window used.

kevin: thanks all. :thumbsup:
